named_events.loss_description: Our net losses from Hurricanes Irma and Michael have reduced since the original estimates and both remain within the ranges we set immediately following the events.
Industry has witnessed considerable deterioration since early evaluation of certain losses arising from natural catastrophes, most notably ... Typhoon Jebi.

We are exposed to Typhoons Faxai and Hagibis through our Property Reinsurance account on the 2019 year following our modest entry into the Japanese reinsurance market. We were cautious in the amount of business written and expect the losses to remain well within our expected level of natural catastrophe activity for the Syndicate.

data.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate shows a gross prior-year strengthening of approximately GBP 7.7m (6.8% of opening gross reserves), derived from the gross claims development table, with the largest adverse development in the 2017 underwriting year. Management commentary notes an overall net prior-year deficit of GBP 1.8m (2018: GBP 9.0m deficit) after reinsurance. The drivers cited include natural catastrophe activity (notably 2017/2018 hurricane and typhoon events) and issues in US casualty claims inflation, partially offset by favourable development in some older years.

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from Statement of Financial Position (prior-year comparative). No explicit gross 'movement in prior years' line was provided; the prior year development gross figure was calculated from the gross claims development table (claims triangle). The Managing Agent narrative reports a net prior-year deficit of GBP 1.8m (net of reinsurance) - that net figure is reported verbatim elsewhere but a gross prior-year movement was not explicitly disclosed, so the triangle was used as the primary source. Amounts are rounded to three decimals (millions).
